documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
61M here to set up primary care. Wants a practice where he can reach the doctor directly; a friend from the cafe he walks to every morning sent him our way.

HPI: Long-standing type 2 diabetes on metformin, blood pressure on lisinopril, cholesterol on atorvastatin. Heart attack in 2016, had a stent put in at that time, and has seen an outside cardiology group roughly once a year since; he thinks his next visit there is summer 2023 but is not sure. Takes a baby aspirin every day since the MI. Gets cramping in both calves after walking a few blocks, eases when he stands a minute; has had that a couple of years and was told it is circulation. Right knee aches with stairs and long days; takes Tylenol when it acts up, avoids anti-inflammatories because the cardiologist told him to. No chest pain, no breathlessness, no palpitations, no fainting. No bleeding.

PMH: T2DM, HTN, hyperlipidemia, CAD s/p MI with stent 2016, PAD with claudication, right knee OA.
PSH: coronary stent 2016.
Meds: aspirin 81 daily; metformin 1000 BID; lisinopril 20 daily; atorvastatin 40 daily; metoprolol succinate 50 daily; acetaminophen 500 1-2 tabs prn.
Allergies: none to medications.
FH: father had a heart attack at 68 and heart surgery around then; mother type 2 diabetes; brother has coronary disease.
SH: retired construction foreman, ran job sites for years. Smoked about a pack a day for close to 30 years, stopped in 2013. Does not drink. Up early, oatmeal, reads the paper, walks to the cafe to see friends. Plays chess. Has grandchildren nearby.

Exam: Vitals as recorded. Comfortable, talkative. Neck supple, no bruits. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Feet: warm, skin intact, no ulcers; dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses diminished both sides; monofilament sensation intact. Right knee: crepitus, no effusion, full extension, flexion to about 110.

A/P:
1. T2DM: A1c today. Metformin continued. Needs eye exam - he goes to an optometrist in town, will ask them to send the report.
2. HTN: 134/80 today, continue lisinopril and metoprolol. CMP.
3. CAD s/p MI/stent, hyperlipidemia: lipids today; continue atorvastatin 40, aspirin, metoprolol. Will get cardiology notes.
4. PAD: claudication stable, encouraged walking program as tolerated.
5. R knee OA: acetaminophen as needed, ok to continue.
6. Former smoker, 30 pk-yr, quit 8 yrs ago: eligible for yearly low-dose CT; ordered, he is agreeable.
7. HM: HCV and HIV screen once today, PHQ-2 negative. Colonoscopy 2019 per patient, records requested. Vaccines - will look at records; flu and pneumococcal in the fall.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Charles, good to meet you on Tuesday. Your labs are back. The A1c, which reflects average sugar over about three months, is 6.9 - right about where we want it. Kidney function, potassium and blood counts are normal and there is no protein leaking into the urine. Cholesterol numbers look reasonable on the atorvastatin. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. No changes to your medicines. The radiology office will call to schedule the lung CT.

OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP - OFFICE NOTE
Date of service: 2023-08-04
Patient: Charles Leblanc, DOB 1960-04-22
Referring/PCP: primary care physician

Reason for visit: annual review of coronary disease and medicines.

Mr. Leblanc is a 63-year-old retired foreman we have followed since his myocardial infarction in 2016, treated with a coronary stent. He has been on the same regimen for years and has had no admissions since. He has continued daily aspirin since the infarct; he bruises a bit easily but tolerates it. He describes cramping in both calves after a few blocks of walking, relieved with rest, unchanged.

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations or syncope. No GI bleeding, black stools or vomiting of blood.

Medications: aspirin 81 mg daily; metformin 1000 mg twice a day; lisinopril 20 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father MI at 68; mother type 2 diabetes; brother with coronary artery disease.
Social: quit cigarettes about ten years ago, roughly 30 pack-years. No alcohol.

Exam: BP 138/78, HR 72, BMI 29. Lungs clear. Regular rhythm, no murmur. Feet warm; dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are reduced on both sides; there is loss of hair over both shins. Otherwise unremarkable.

Data: lipids from last week - LDL 82 mg/dL, HDL 46 mg/dL. Hemoglobin and platelet count normal. ECG today: sinus rhythm, normal.

Assessment:
1. Coronary artery disease, remote MI with stent, no angina.
2. Peripheral arterial disease with stable claudication.
3. Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes - managed by PCP.
4. Long-term aspirin, minor bruising only.

Plan: no changes. Continue aspirin, statin, beta-blocker and ACE inhibitor. Follow up in one year or sooner for symptoms.

Electronically signed, cardiology attending.

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Booked as a diabetes check; the main thing today is his chest.

HPI: 64M with CAD, MI and stent in 2016, last saw cardiology a year ago and was told all was stable. Over the past month or so he gets a tight, heavy feeling across the chest when he walks up the hill on the way home from the cafe or carries groceries up the porch steps. Stops, stands a couple of minutes, it goes. Never at rest, never woken by it. Has happened maybe eight or ten times. No sweats, no fainting, no palpitations. Says it feels "like a smaller version" of 2016. No cough, cold or fever lately; no other complaints. Taking all his meds.

Meds: aspirin 81, metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.

Exam: BP 142/88, HR 78, BMI 32 (weight up again). Not in distress. JVP not elevated. Heart regular, no murmurs, rubs or gallops. Lungs clear. No edema. Pedal pulses diminished as before.

ECG in office: sinus, no acute ST changes, no Q waves; unchanged from cardiology's 2023 tracing.

Labs 7/24: A1c 7.2, fasting glucose 158, TC 190, LDL 100, HDL 40, TG 150, creatinine 1.1.

A/P:
1. Exertional chest pain in a man with known CAD - stable angina pattern, no rest pain, ECG unchanged. Managing medically for now on his current beta-blocker, statin and aspirin; referral back to his cardiologist for evaluation, asked them to see him promptly. Reviewed red flags: pain at rest, lasting more than a few minutes, or with sweating or breathlessness - call 911.
2. DM2 - A1c 7.2, a little higher. Continue metformin.
3. HTN - 142/88 today; no change for now, recheck at next visit.
4. Hyperlipidemia - LDL 100 on atorvastatin 40; continue.
5. Obesity, BMI 32 - weight gain since last year tied to less walking with the knee. Brief counseling.
6. PAD, R knee OA - unchanged.
Lung CT due August, ordered.

CARDIOLOGY CLINIC NOTE
Visit date: 2025-02-10
Re: Charles Leblanc, 1960-04-22
To: primary care physician - thank you for sending him back.

HPI: Seen here 18 months ago with stable coronary disease. Since last summer he has had chest pressure with exertion, settling with rest, as described in your July note; that has continued. What is new over the past several months is breathlessness on climbing a flight of stairs, which he did not have when you saw him in July. No rest symptoms, no syncope.

Meds: aspirin 81 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg. NKDA.

Exam: BP 142/88, HR 78, BMI 32. Regular rhythm. Lungs clear.

Data reviewed: your labs of 7/24/24 - A1c 7.2%, TC 190, LDL 100, HDL 40, TG 150, creatinine 1.1. ECG today without acute ST change or Q waves.

Impression: stable angina with new exertional dyspnea in a patient with prior MI and stent - concerning for progression of coronary disease.

Plan: exercise treadmill stress test in the next few weeks. Continue current antianginal and secondary prevention regimen in the meantime. Will contact him with results and next steps.

Cardiology attending

reports.text: Indication: exertional chest pain and dyspnea, known CAD. Protocol: Bruce. Resting ECG sinus rhythm without ST abnormality. Exercise stopped early in stage 1 for chest pressure and breathlessness. At that low workload there was significant horizontal ST-segment depression in multiple leads, resolving in recovery. Blood pressure rose appropriately. No arrhythmia.
reports.conclusion: Positive for ischemia: significant ST depression at low workload. High-risk result; angiography to be considered.

documents.title: Cardiology pre-operative evaluation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY - PRE-OPERATIVE CONSULTATION
Date seen: 2025-08-04
Patient: Charles Leblanc, 65
cc: primary care physician; cardiac surgery

He returns after cardiac catheterization. His exertional angina has been treated medically on metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin 40 mg and lisinopril, and it has not settled: he still gets chest pain with exertion and now has occasional episodes at rest. The March treadmill test showed marked ST depression at a low workload. Coronary angiography on 7/21 showed severe disease of all three major coronary arteries, not suitable for a percutaneous approach; surgical revascularization is recommended.

PMH: CAD with MI and stent 2016; type 2 diabetes; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; PAD; severe osteoarthritis of the knee, with a knee replacement anticipated after he recovers.
Meds: aspirin 81 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily. NKDA.
FH: his father had a heart attack and heart surgery at 68; he remembers visiting him in the hospital.
SH: former smoker, quit about 12 years ago. No alcohol. Retired construction foreman.

He is frank that surgery frightens him, but he wants more years with his grandchildren and has decided to go ahead.

Exam: Vital signs stable. BMI 31. Soft S4. Mild pitting edema at both ankles. Peripheral pulses present but diminished. Lungs clear.

Labs (7/21): hemoglobin 12.4 g/dL - mild anemia; HbA1c 7.6%.
Echo 7/21: LVEF 38%, anterior wall hypokinesis.
Cath 7/21: severe three-vessel coronary artery disease.

Assessment: stable angina due to coronary artery disease, three-vessel, refractory to medical therapy, with reduced LV function.

Plan: referral accepted by cardiac surgery for CABG; the surgeon met him today and explained that a vein from the leg will be taken for the grafts, with the incision placed along known landmarks, and he agreed to proceed. Continue all current medications until surgery; the surgical team will give peri-operative instructions. We will see him after recovery.

Cardiology attending

documents.title: Discharge summary - cardiac surgery
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - CARDIAC SURGERY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 2025-09-09  Discharged: 2025-09-14
Patient: Charles Leblanc, DOB 1960-04-22
Allergies: NKDA

Admitting diagnosis: severe three-vessel coronary artery disease with stable angina refractory to medical therapy; LVEF 38%.
Procedure 9/9/25: coronary artery bypass grafting x3 - left internal mammary artery graft and two reverse saphenous vein grafts, vein harvested from the right leg. Cardiopulmonary bypass. No intraoperative complications.

Hospital course: extubated the evening of surgery. Chest tubes removed POD 2. Remained in sinus rhythm. Glucose monitored closely; metformin resumed at discharge. Mobilizing in the halls by POD 3. Sternal and leg incisions clean and dry. Hemoglobin 10.8 on the day of discharge, expected post-operative; no transfusion.

Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; metformin 1000 mg twice daily.

Follow-up: cardiac surgery wound check 2 weeks; cardiology 2 months; outpatient cardiac rehabilitation referral placed; primary care within 1-2 weeks.
Instructions: sternal precautions, no driving 4 weeks, no lifting over 10 lb for 6 weeks.

Cardiac surgery attending

documents.title: Discharge summary filed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Discharge summary arrived today, three weeks after discharge. Matches what he told us. Hgb 10.8 at discharge. Recheck CBC at next visit.

documents.title: Pt home after bypass
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called: had his bypass 9/9, home since Sunday. Three grafts, he says. Sore chest, using a pillow to cough, walking in the house and driveway. No fever, incisions dry. Taking the same five pills as before. No discharge paperwork has reached us - asked him to bring his packet to the visit. Booked post-hospital visit 9/23 with PCP. Records request sent to the hospital.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks after three-vessel bypass, here with his discharge folder (the hospital's summary has not reached us yet; his folder has the med list and instructions).

He is doing better than he expected. Chest wall soreness, improving; acetaminophen only. Walking 10 minutes twice a day. No chest pressure like before, no breathlessness at rest, sleeping in bed. Appetite low; down a few kilos. Leg incision a little tender. Rehab intake is booked for next week.

Meds (reconciled with the folder): aspirin 81, metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, acetaminophen prn - unchanged from before surgery. NKDA.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Sternal incision healing, no drainage, sternum stable. Right leg vein-harvest incision clean, mild bruising along it. Heart regular, no rub. Lungs clear.

A/P:
- S/p CABG x3: recovering well. Added to problem list. Continue all meds; cardiac rehab; surgeon follow-up next week; cardiology in November.
- DM2: sugars running 130s-150s at home per his log. Metformin.
- Anemia after surgery per his folder: CBC at the December visit.
See in 2-3 months.

reports.text: Post-CABG reassessment. Comparison 2025-07-21. Left ventricle normal in size. LVEF estimated 50%, improved. Mild hypokinesis of the anterior wall. Right ventricular size and function normal. Valves without significant disease. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: LVEF 50%, improved from 38%; mild anterior hypokinesis.

CARDIOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date: 2025-11-17
Charles Leblanc, 65. Ten weeks after CABG x3.

He is without angina. Climbing stairs again without stopping. Halfway through cardiac rehabilitation and enjoying it. Incisions healed.

Medications: aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID.

Exam: regular rhythm, no murmur or rub. Lungs clear. No edema.

Echo today: LVEF 50%, mild anterior hypokinesis - improved after revascularization.

Assessment: CAD s/p CABG, doing well; LV function improved.
Plan: continue current regimen without change. Finish rehab. From our standpoint he may plan the knee replacement once he is 6 months out from surgery. Return in 6 months.

Cardiology attending

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months after bypass. Heart-wise he feels the best he has in two years - no chest pressure, does the rehab bike and treadmill without symptoms. Cardiology saw him in November, echo better, no changes.

The problem now is the right knee. More walking for rehab has made it much worse: aching most days, grinding, stiff after sitting, hard on stairs going down. Acetaminophen takes the edge off. Cardiology told him no anti-inflammatories, which he follows. No locking, no falls.

Exam: vitals reviewed, BP better than last year. Sternum healed. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema. Right knee: crepitus throughout motion, bony enlargement, flexion to about 100, no effusion, no warmth.

A/P:
1. Right knee OA, now severe clinically - x-ray today, refer to orthopedics to discuss replacement (cardiology says ok to plan after the 6-month mark). Continue acetaminophen.
2. S/p CABG: doing well; continue all meds.
3. DM2: A1c drawn, metformin.
4. Post-op anemia: CBC today.
5. HTN: fine.
Physical in April.

reports.text: Right knee, three views including standing AP. Marked narrowing of the medial joint space with marginal osteophytes and subchondral sclerosis. Lateral and patellofemoral compartments relatively preserved. No fracture. No joint effusion. Soft tissues unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Advanced medial compartment osteoarthritis of the right knee.

documents.title: Your x-ray and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Charles - the knee x-ray shows advanced wear-and-tear arthritis on the inner side of the right knee, which fits with how much it is bothering you. The orthopedic office has the referral and should call you. Blood count is recovering nicely after surgery (12.9, up from 10.8). A1c 7.4, a little higher than before surgery - not unusual after a big operation; we'll look again in the spring. Kidney function normal.

65 (66 next week). Annual exam, fasting.

Seven months out from bypass. Finished cardiac rehab in December and kept going at the rehab gym twice a week until the knee made the treadmill too painful; now uses the bike. No angina, no dyspnea on stairs. Knee surgery planned for July 31 with orthopedics; consult note still not received. Weight creeping back up. Mood good, PHQ-2 0. No falls.

Meds: aspirin 81, metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.

Exam: well. Eyes, ears, mouth normal. No carotid bruit. Healed sternotomy. Heart regular, no murmur or gallop. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no pulsatile mass. No edema. Feet: diminished pedal pulses as always, sensation intact, skin fine. Right knee as in December.

Plan:
- Fasting CMP, lipids, urine albumin today. A1c with the pre-op labs in June.
- One-time abdominal aortic ultrasound (male, former smoker, 65) - ordered.
- Lung CT skipped last year during the heart workup; ordered now. Still within 15 years of quitting.
- Colonoscopy due 2029. Vaccines current; flu/COVID in fall.
- Pre-op visit in June for the knee.
All meds continued.

documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
To the orthopedic surgeon and primary care physician:

Re: Charles Leblanc, DOB 1960-04-22. Planned right total knee arthroplasty, 2026-07-31.

Mr. Leblanc is nine months out from three-vessel bypass surgery with an uneventful recovery. He has had no angina since the operation, and his ejection fraction improved to 50% on the November echo. Functional capacity is limited by the knee rather than by his heart.

From a cardiac standpoint he is at acceptable risk for the planned procedure. Please continue aspirin, atorvastatin and metoprolol through the peri-operative period. No further cardiac testing is needed before surgery.

Cardiology attending

documents.title: Pre-operative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pre-op H&P for elective right total knee arthroplasty, 7/31/26, orthopedic surgery.

HPI: 66M with severe right knee OA, failed conservative care (acetaminophen, activity changes, home exercise). CAD s/p MI with stent 2016 and CABG x3 9/2025, EF improved to 50%. No angina since bypass; can climb a flight of stairs without chest symptoms, limited only by the knee. No orthopnea, no palpitations, no syncope. No bleeding problems besides easy bruising on aspirin. No prior problems with anesthesia during the bypass. Cardiology clearance letter 6/10 on file.

PMH: DM2, HTN, hyperlipidemia, CAD/old MI/stent, s/p CABG, PAD, obesity, R knee OA.
Meds: aspirin 81 daily, metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, metoprolol succinate 50 daily, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.
SH: former smoker, quit 2013. No alcohol.

Exam: vitals as charted. Airway: good mouth opening, full neck motion. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Healed sternotomy and right leg incisions. No edema. Right knee: crepitus, no effusion, skin intact without breaks or infection.

Data: ECG today sinus rhythm, no acute changes. CBC, BMP, A1c drawn.

Assessment: acceptable risk for planned surgery from a medical standpoint; cardiac risk addressed by cardiology.
Recommendations:
- Continue aspirin, atorvastatin and metoprolol, including the morning of surgery, per cardiology.
- Hold metformin and lisinopril the morning of surgery; resume when eating and drinking.
- Glucose monitoring peri-operatively.
- VTE prophylaxis and antibiotic prophylaxis per the surgical team.
Will fax this note and labs to orthopedics once results are back.
Follow up in September after recovery.

documents.title: Pre-op labs and clearance
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt with pre-op results per PCP: hemoglobin 13.6, back to normal; A1c 7.2; kidneys and potassium normal. Clearance note, ECG and labs faxed to orthopedic surgery, confirmation received. Pt aware to hold metformin and lisinopril the morning of 7/31. Post-op follow-up booked 9/15.

documents.title: Operative report - right total knee arthroplasty
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT - ORTHOPEDIC SURGERY
Date of surgery: 2026-07-31
Patient: Charles Leblanc, 66, DOB 1960-04-22
Allergies: no known drug allergies

Pre-operative diagnosis: severe primary osteoarthritis, right knee.
Post-operative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: right total knee arthroplasty, cemented.

Pre-operative assessment: BP 135/85, HR 78, BMI 32. Right knee without erythema, warmth or any sign of infection; marked joint space narrowing on imaging and crepitus through range of motion. Pre-admission labs within normal limits. Medical and cardiology clearance on file. Home medications: aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, metformin, lisinopril.

Antibiotic prophylaxis: cefazolin 2 g IV given within 60 minutes before incision for surgical site infection prophylaxis.
Anesthesia: spinal with sedation; adductor canal block.

Description: Tourniquet applied. Medial parapatellar approach. Advanced medial compartment wear with full-thickness cartilage loss and osteophytes confirmed. Standard femoral and tibial cuts, ligament balancing, cemented femoral and tibial components with patellar resurfacing. Wound irrigated and closed in layers. Sterile dressing. Estimated blood loss 150 mL. No complications.

Post-operative course: walked with physical therapy on the day of surgery. Discharged home 2026-08-02 with home physical therapy.
Discharge plan: weight bearing as tolerated; aspirin 81 mg twice daily for 4 weeks for clot prevention, then back to once daily; oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 one tablet every 6 hours as needed for severe pain; ice and elevation. Staple removal and follow-up in clinic at 2 weeks.

Orthopedic surgery attending
